items.title: Geometric electrovac data solve the selected SI equations
items.physical_scope: Conditional conversion of a smooth zero-cosmological-constant geometric electrovac datum to the source-free branch of the selected SI equation-based Einstein–Maxwell model. It does not assert existence of geometric data, derive or empirically validate a postulate, add material sources, or claim physical realization.
items.design_state: Locally added A-page intermediate theorem for the shared geometric-to-SI normalization; complete proof and dependency review are recorded in batch-25 evidence.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ be a smooth source-free geometric electrovac datum
of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] on a nonempty smooth four-manifold.
Thus $g$ has signature $(-,+,+,+)$, $\mathcal F$ is a smooth real two-form,
and
$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F),\qquad Q_{ab}(X):=X_{ac}X_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}X_{cd}X^{cd}.$$
Choose constants $G_N,c,\mu_0>0$ in the SI roles of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]], set
$$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1},\qquad \alpha=\sqrt{\frac{4\pi G_N}{\mu_0c^4}},\qquad F:=\alpha^{-1}\mathcal F,$$
and use the same metric and orientation for $F$. In length coordinates
$x^0=ct$, $F_{ab}$ has units T, $\mathcal F_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$,
and $\alpha$ has units $\mathrm{T}^{-1}\mathrm{m}^{-1}$ by
[[def-emg-xs-si-parameters]]. Define
$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}Q_{ab}(F),\qquad \kappa_E:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}.$$
In the adopted postulate [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]], specialize
to $\Lambda=0$, $j=0$, and $T^m=0$. Then
$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla^g_aF^{ab}=0,\qquad G_{ab}=\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}.$$
This is a conditional model deduction: it neither derives the postulate nor
claims that the model describes nature.

items.title: Harmonic static multicenter electrovac model
items.physical_scope: Conditional source-free classical Einstein–Maxwell model on the smooth exterior of finitely many removed centers, with a common electric sign and positive selected SI mass parameters. Fluxes are through regular spheres. No source is asserted at an excluded center; no horizon extension, completeness, stability, black-hole realization, observation, or empirical validity is claimed.
items.design_state: Authored from the planned claim with exact model hypotheses, conditional supplier status, and warnings retained.
items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$ be finite, let $a_1,\ldots,a_N\in\mathbb R^3$ be distinct
length-coordinate points, choose SI mass parameters $m_{*,A}>0$, and fix one
sign $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$. Set
$$m_A:=\frac{G_Nm_{*,A}}{c^2},\qquad D:=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{a_1,\ldots,a_N\},\qquad H(x):=1+\sum_{A=1}^N\frac{m_A}{|x-a_A|}.$$
The positive length parameters $m_A$ make $H$ dimensionless and smooth
positive harmonic on $D$. The future unit field is $N_H=H\partial_{x^0}$,
with $g_H(N_H,N_H)=-1$. Here static means the metric coefficients are
independent of $x^0$, have no $dx^0dx^i$ terms, and are invariant under
$x^0\mapsto-x^0$; the displayed metric has all three properties. On
$\mathcal M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$, with
$x^0=ct$ and the orientation of [[def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp]], take
$$g_H=-H^{-2}(dx^0)^2+H^2\delta_{ij}dx^i dx^j,\qquad \mathcal A_\sigma=\sigma(H^{-1}-1)dx^0,\qquad \mathcal F_\sigma=d\mathcal A_\sigma,\qquad F:=\alpha^{-1}\mathcal F_\sigma,$$
where $\alpha=\sqrt{4\pi G_N/(\mu_0c^4)}$ as in
[[def-emg-xs-si-parameters]]. Under the adopted equation-based model of
[[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] with $\Lambda=0$, $j=0$, and
$T^m=0$, these data satisfy the source-free SI equations
$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla^g_aF^{ab}=0,\qquad G_{ab}=\kappa_ET^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}.$$
For each $A$ and $r>0$, define the coordinate sphere and its closed ball by
$$S_A(r):=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x-a_A|=r\}.$$

$$\overline B_A(r):=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x-a_A|\le r\}.$$
Orient $S_A(r)$ by its outward unit normal relative to the standard orientation
of $\mathbb R^3$.
For every such sphere $S\subset D$, fix any $s\in\mathbb R_{x^0}$ and use
$i_{s,S}:S\hookrightarrow\mathcal M$, $i_{s,S}(x)=(s,x)$, with the
transported outward orientation. Every flux written over $S$ below means
the integral of the spacetime form pulled back by $i_{s,S}$; by
[[prop-emg-xs-mp-multicenter]] these values are independent of $s$.
Whenever $\overline B_A(r)$ contains no other center, the geometric fluxes are
$$q_e(S_A(r))=\sigma m_A,\qquad q_m(S_A(r))=0.$$
The corresponding SI electric-flux parameter is
$$Q_{e,A}:=\varepsilon_0c\int_{S_A(r)}\star_gF =\sigma\sqrt{4\pi\varepsilon_0G_N}\,m_{*,A},$$
and its magnetic flux $\int_{S_A(r)}F$ is zero. Define the outward-oriented
origin-centered sphere by $S_R:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=R\}$, where the
orientation is induced by the outward unit normal relative to the standard
orientation of $\mathbb R^3$. For $R>\max_A|a_A|$, it has
the sum of these electric fluxes. These
are model parameters and regular-sphere fluxes, not measurements or evidence
of regular material sources at the removed points.

items.title: Single-center extremal charged model correspondence
items.physical_scope: Equality of the single-center harmonic MP and electric extremal RN model data on their open exteriors under one explicit SI mass/charge parametrization. No horizon extension, global completeness, source at the omitted center, ADM or Komar identification, observed object, or empirical validity is asserted.

items.statement:
Let $m_*>0$ be a selected SI mass parameter, choose $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$,
and set
$$m:=\frac{G_Nm_*}{c^2},\qquad Q_e:=\sigma\sqrt{4\pi\varepsilon_0G_N}\,m_*,\qquad \Phi_B:=0.$$
Use $\alpha=\sqrt{4\pi G_N/(\mu_0c^4)}$ and the parameter map of
[[def-emg-xs-si-parameters]]. On the single-center MP exterior
$D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $H=1+m/|x|$, the change of radial
coordinate $R=|x|+m$ identifies the SI metric and field
$F=\alpha^{-1}\mathcal F_\sigma$ exactly with the electric RN data of
[[def-emg-xs-rn-data]] on $R>m$, with
$$M=m,\qquad q_e=\sigma m,\qquad q_m=0,\qquad f(R)=\left(1-\frac mR\right)^2.$$
Thus $|q_e|=M$ and the two presentations describe the same source-free
solution of the adopted zero-$\Lambda$ equation-based model on that open
exterior. The correspondence does not extend the coordinate map to $R=m$.

items.title: Constant-radius charged product model
items.physical_scope: Conditional source-free SI model on either specified open Bertotti–Robinson product chart, with constant sphere radius L>0 and the specified smooth nonzero two-form. No maximal extension, asymptotic-flatness, source at a boundary, observation, or empirical realization is asserted.
items.design_state: Authored from the planned claim with exact model hypotheses, conditional supplier status, and warnings retained.
items.statement:
Let $L>0$ be a length. Choose either the product chart with dimensionless
coordinates $\tau,z$, $z\in J$ for a nonempty open $J\subset(0,\infty)$ and
$f(z)=z^2$, or the chart with $z\in J$ for a nonempty open
$J\subset\mathbb R$ and $f(z)=1+z^2$. Take the metric and geometric
field of [[def-emg-xs-br-products]]:
$$g_{L,f}=L^2\left(-f(z)d\tau^2+f(z)^{-1}dz^2+\gamma_{S^2}\right),\qquad \mathcal F_L=-L\,d\tau\wedge dz.$$
For $G_N,c,\mu_0>0$, set $\alpha=\sqrt{4\pi G_N/(\mu_0c^4)}$ and
$F_L=\alpha^{-1}\mathcal F_L$. Under the adopted postulate
[[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] with $\Lambda=0$, $j=0$, and $T^m=0$,
the SI field $F_L$ and metric $g_{L,f}$ satisfy
$$dF_L=0,\qquad \nabla^g_aF_L^{ab}=0,\qquad G_{ab}=\kappa_ET^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}.$$
The sphere factor has radius $L$ at each base point. This is a deduction for
the stated open charts only.

items.title: Local SI model limit from extremal RN to Bertotti–Robinson
items.physical_scope: Exact local smooth scaling limit of the selected electric extremal RN exterior to the Poincaré product chart of the source-free Einstein–Maxwell model. Convergence is only on compact subsets of R>0; no extension through the limiting boundary, global limit, or empirical claim is included.
items.design_state: Authored from the planned claim with exact model hypotheses, conditional supplier status, and warnings retained.
items.statement:
Fix $L>0$. Select
$$m_*=\frac{c^2L}{G_N},\qquad Q_e=+\sqrt{4\pi\varepsilon_0G_N}\,m_*,\qquad \Phi_B=0.$$
The map of [[def-emg-xs-si-parameters]] gives $M=q_e=L$, $q_m=0$, so the electric
RN metric function is $f(r)=(1-L/r)^2$ on $r>L$. For every dimensionless
$\lambda>0$, on $\mathbb R_T\times(0,\infty)_R\times S^2$ define
$$\Phi_\lambda(T,R,\omega)=(x^0=T/\lambda,\ r=L+\lambda R,\ \omega).$$
Let $g_\lambda=\Phi_\lambda^*g$ and
$F_\lambda=\Phi_\lambda^*F$ for the SI extremal RN solution. Then
$$g_\lambda=-\frac{R^2}{(L+\lambda R)^2}dT^2+ \frac{(L+\lambda R)^2}{R^2}dR^2+(L+\lambda R)^2\gamma_{S^2},$$
and $F_\lambda=\alpha^{-1}\mathcal F_\lambda$ where
$$\mathcal F_\lambda=-\frac{L}{(L+\lambda R)^2}dT\wedge dR.$$
As $\lambda\downarrow0$, $(g_\lambda,F_\lambda)$ converges in
$C^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}$ on $\mathbb R_T\times(0,\infty)_R\times S^2$ to
$$g_0=-\frac{R^2}{L^2}dT^2+\frac{L^2}{R^2}dR^2+L^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad F_0=-\frac{1}{\alpha L}dT\wedge dR.$$
Under $T=L\tau$ and $R=Lz$, the limit is exactly the electric
Bertotti–Robinson data of [[def-emg-xs-br-products]] with $f(z)=z^2$, $z>0$.
By [[pthm-emg-xs-br-model]], it is a solution of the same adopted SI model.
The convergence and solution statements are limited to the stated open
domains and do not assert an extension at $R=0$.

items.title: Exact coupled electromagnetic null-wave model
items.physical_scope: Exact source-free classical SI Einstein–Maxwell solutions on the specified plane-fronted null-wave chart, for arbitrary smooth electromagnetic profiles and smooth transverse harmonic gravitational profile. No asymptotic flatness, finite total energy, observation, or empirical validity is asserted.
items.design_state: Authored from the planned claim with exact model hypotheses, conditional supplier status, and warnings retained.
items.statement:
Use length coordinates $(u,v,x,y)$ on $\mathbb R^4$. Let
$a,b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth profiles with units
$\mathrm{m}^{-1}$, and let $h:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be smooth,
dimensionless, and satisfy $h_{xx}+h_{yy}=0$. Set
$$P(u,x,y)=-(a(u)^2+b(u)^2)(x^2+y^2)+h(u,x,y),$$
$$g=-2\,du\,dv+dx^2+dy^2+P\,du^2,\qquad \mathcal A=-(a(u)x+b(u)y)\,du,$$
$$\mathcal F=d\mathcal A=a(u)\,du\wedge dx+b(u)\,du\wedge dy,\qquad F=\alpha^{-1}\mathcal F,$$
where $\alpha=\sqrt{4\pi G_N/(\mu_0c^4)}$ from
[[def-emg-xs-si-parameters]]. Use the orientation $du\wedge dv\wedge dx\wedge dy$ and future unit field
$N=\partial_u+(P+1)\partial_v/2$, as in
[[def-emg-xs-null-wave]]. The metric has signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Under the adopted postulate
[[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] with no material stress or current and
$\Lambda=0$, these data satisfy the source-free SI Einstein–Maxwell equations
on all of $\mathbb R^4$. The claim is an exact model deduction; it asserts
neither asymptotic flatness nor finite total wave energy.

items.title: Nonzero null-wave field and curvature with four specified scalar contractions vanishing
items.physical_scope: Hypothetical exact null-wave solution of the selected classical SI Einstein–Maxwell model, specialized to one nonzero constant transverse profile. It illustrates a pointwise tensor distinction only and makes no observation, finite-energy, asymptotic-flatness, or empirical-validity claim.
items.design_state: Authored from the planned claim with exact model hypotheses, conditional supplier status, and warnings retained.
items.statement:
Choose a constant $\nu>0$ with units $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$ and the profiles
$a(u)=\nu$, $b(u)=0$, $h(u,x,y)=0$ in
[[def-emg-xs-null-wave]]. Then
$$P=-\nu^2(x^2+y^2),\qquad g=-2\,du\,dv+dx^2+dy^2-\nu^2(x^2+y^2)du^2,$$
$$\mathcal F=\nu\,du\wedge dx,\qquad F=\alpha^{-1}\mathcal F.$$
Use orientation $du\wedge dv\wedge dx\wedge dy$ and future unit field
$N=\partial_u+(P+1)\partial_v/2$ from the null-wave definition. This is a smooth source-free solution of the adopted SI model of
[[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] by
[[pthm-emg-xs-null-wave-model]]. Its electromagnetic field is nonzero.
Define the scalar curvature by $S:=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, using the
curvature convention of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. Then
$$F_{ab}F^{ab}=0,\qquad S=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}\operatorname{Ric}^{ab}=0,\qquad R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=0.$$
At the same time $R_{uxux}=\nu^2\ne0$, so the spacetime is not flat. These
zero scalar contractions therefore do not imply a vanishing electromagnetic
field or flat spacetime. This is a hypothetical model calculation, not an
observation.

items.title: Two-center ideal static charged configuration
items.physical_scope: Hypothetical two-center exact source-free SI model on the punctured exterior, with two selected positive SI mass parameters and one common sign for both electric flux parameters. Excluded centers are not included as sources or regular points. No horizon extension, stability, observed configuration, or empirical-validity claim is made.
items.design_state: Authored from the planned claim with exact model hypotheses, conditional supplier status, and warnings retained.
items.statement:
Let $d>0$ be the separation of the centers, measured in metres, and let
$m_{*,1},m_{*,2}>0$ be selected SI masses. Put $a_1=(0,0,0)$, $a_2=(d,0,0)$, choose one sign
$\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$, and set $m_A=G_Nm_{*,A}/c^2$ for $A=1,2$. On
$D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{a_1,a_2\}$ take
$$H(x)=1+\frac{m_1}{|x-a_1|}+\frac{m_2}{|x-a_2|},$$
and define the spheres with outward Euclidean orientation by
$$S_A(r):=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x-a_A|=r\}\quad(0<r<d/2).$$

$$S_R:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=R\}\quad(R>d).$$

$$g_H=-H^{-2}(dx^0)^2+H^2\delta_{ij}dx^i dx^j,\qquad \mathcal A_\sigma=\sigma(H^{-1}-1)dx^0,\qquad F=\alpha^{-1}d\mathcal A_\sigma,$$
with $x^0=ct$ and $\alpha$ from [[def-emg-xs-si-parameters]]. This hypothetical
datum solves the selected source-free SI model on $\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$.
For every displayed sphere $S$, use $i_{s,S}(x)=(s,x)$ into
$\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$ at any fixed $s$, with transported outward
orientation, as in [[prop-emg-xs-mp-multicenter]] and
[[pthm-emg-xs-mp-model]]. Each integral over $S$ means the integral of
the spacetime form pulled back by $i_{s,S}$ and is independent of $s$.
For each $S_A(r)$, its SI electric flux is
$$\varepsilon_0c\int_{S_A(r)}\star_gF =\sigma\sqrt{4\pi\varepsilon_0G_N}\,m_{*,A},$$
and its magnetic flux is zero. On $S_R$, the electric flux is the sum of the two displayed values and
the magnetic flux remains zero. The example is a model calculation; it does
not insert a source at either omitted point or claim that two observed
black holes are in equilibrium.
